period_note: SOLO basis, from this bank's own real Q2/Half-Yearly 2020 interim financial statement. Balance sheet is the 30-Jun-2020 snapshot. Primary income-statement line items (no suffix) are the DISCRETE Apr-Jun 2020 quarter, taken directly from this filing's own 'April'20-June'20' column (not derived by subtracting Q1 from a cumulative figure). '_cumulative' suffixed items are the Jan-Jun 2020 6-month figures from the same filing's 'Jan'20-Jun'20' column. See the tax_expense/profit_after_tax note for a specific, narrow discrepancy against the annual report's later retrospective table. non_interest_income here EXCLUDES investment_income (they are separate line items in this quarter's real interim statement), matching the Q4/annual files' definition of non_interest_income -- NOT the broader bundled definition used in this dataset's table-only years (2014-2019), which folds investment income into 'non_interest_income'.

source.source_page_lines: Solo Balance Sheet p.13-14 and Profit and Loss Account p.15 of the PDF

DISCREPANCY vs the FY2020 annual report's own later retrospective 'Quarterly Performance' table: this contemporaneous interim filing states discrete Apr-Jun 2020 Tax Effect as 76.02 and Net profit as 165.73; the annual report's retrospective table instead shows 85.54 and 156.33 for the same quarter (a 9.4-9.5m gap, ~6%). Every OTHER row for this quarter reconciles between the two sources to within rounding (Net Interest Income 224.32 exact match, Total Operating Income 958.59 exact match, Provisions 71.41 exact match, Operating Expenses 645.31 vs 645.42). The divergence is isolated to the tax line and its flow-through to net profit. Per this dataset's standing rule, the contemporaneous (interim, unaudited-at-the-time) figure is kept here and the later retrospective figure is recorded as the divergence, not the other way round.
